books.label: Beauty and the Beast
books.title: Beauty and the Beast
books.author: Gabrielle-Suzanne de Villeneuve
books.blurb: A merchant’s daughter trades her freedom for her father’s life and finds a castle where nothing is quite what it appears.
books.blurb2: Villeneuve’s 1740 novella is longer and stranger than the versions that reached the screen: the Beast has a history, the household has opinions, and the ending is earned rather than granted.

books.label: Fire and Blood
books.title: Fire and Blood
books.author: George RR Martin
books.blurb: The Targaryen conquest told as history rather than saga: Aegon’s landing, the dragons that made it possible, and the succession wars that followed.
books.blurb2: Martin writes this one as an archmaester would, with competing sources and gaps in the record. The effect is a dynasty that reads like a real one, which is exactly the point.

books.label: The Chronicles of Narnia
books.title: The Chronicles of Narnia
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.blurb: Seven books that start with a wardrobe and end with the country itself, moving from children’s adventure to something closer to myth.
books.blurb2: Reading the series in one volume makes the structure visible: each book retells a different kind of story, and the last one re-reads everything before it.
books.edition: Paperback omnibus, 768 pages in this copy.

books.label: Deadpool Samurai
books.title: Deadpool Samurai
books.author: Marvel
books.blurb: Deadpool takes a job in Japan, joins a hero agency, and discovers that manga rules apply to him whether he agrees to them or not.
books.blurb2: The gag rate is the point. Every chapter runs a new genre through the character, and the art keeps the action clean enough that the jokes land.

books.label: Harry Potter 06
books.title: Harry Potter: Half-Blood Prince
books.author: J.K. Rowling
books.blurb: Harry’s sixth year at Hogwarts turns on memory: whose past gets recovered, whose is sealed, and what it costs to learn the truth about Voldemort.
books.blurb2: Rowling uses the Pensieve as the book’s engine: the plot advances by recovering other people’s pasts, and the cost of that knowledge lands on the people who asked for it.

books.label: The Lost Hero
books.title: The Lost Hero
books.author: Rick Riordan
books.blurb: Jason wakes on a school bus with no memory of who he is, and the only two people who claim to know him are strangers with a quest.
books.blurb2: Riordan starts a second series by changing the camera: the Roman camp exists, the Greek camp exists, and neither has been telling the other the whole story.

books.label: A Game of Thrones
books.title: A Game of Thrones
books.author: George RR Martin
books.blurb: A Hand dies, a king rides north, and five families start treating a peace as an opening rather than a fact.
books.blurb2: The first volume is a long setup that never feels like one: every chapter shifts the balance, and the rules of who survives are set early and kept.

books.label: The Hobbit
books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.series: Prelude to The Lord of the Rings
books.blurb: A comfortable hobbit is talked into an uncomfortable journey by a wizard, thirteen dwarves, and a contract he does not read closely.
books.blurb2: Written for children and read by everyone else: the tone is lighter than the trilogy, but the ending already knows what a long war costs.
